utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djurasic. May I remind you of the affirmation that you took at the beginning which still applies. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djurasic. We are going to continue with the examination-in-chief. You mentioned yesterday during the examination-in-chief that Mr. Ivo Simunovic from Dubrovnik came to Mokosica on a number of occasions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did he come -- in what capacity, to put it that way, did he come to Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came for talks with me in the capacity of the representative of the town of Dubrovnik and their army, the army that was in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was he secure? Was security provided when he came to Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you please make pauses between my question and your answer for interpretation purposes. Thank you. Did Mr. Simunovic perhaps call you to come to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion he did offer to have the talks held in Dubrovnik, and I accepted his invitation. However, when he told me that I would have to come wearing civilian clothes, I didn't want to. I wanted to wear my uniform just as he wore his uniform when he came to see me. He said he couldn't guarantee my safety and security, so I never actually went.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Simunovic on the side where the JNA was, did he have any property there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He had his house in Zaton. And on one occasion, he came to visit his house, and on another occasion he brought a foreign delegation also to show them his property. I received them. I saw them off and returned safely. And so did he.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did he have any problems with that property that he owned there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came for the first time, the family house, it was a family house where his mother lived. That was completely intact and untouched. However, when he came on the second occasion, it had been looted, and the goods inside the house had been disturbed. I explained to him that it was probably that some of our soldiers saw him go to the house and that is why they upset the things that were inside. But he had a look round quickly, and as far as he could see nothing had been taken away, although everything had been in a shambles.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the exact location of his family house. Give us a location.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's in Zatan. The place is called Zatan. I can't give you the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to call upon the usher to distribute a document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djurasic, do you recognise this document, if you look at the title, the heading on page two of the document, whose document it is?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a document of the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector, the 9th VPS, deputy commander for morale and propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And who is the document addressed to?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is addressed to the command of the place called Grude. I don't know who in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At that time, were you at the command post at Grude doing your duty there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the document, perhaps read through it briefly, and tell us whether the contents are familiar.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite franks, it's difficult for me to remember this document precisely because there were quite a number of documents of this kind where it said information, so I can't pinpoint this particular one and say yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, if you take a look at paragraph 2, perhaps, where it says that an agreement with Croatia was signed and that it provided for the fact that by the 10th of December 1991, a complete relocation of manpower, equipment, materiel, ammunition, mines, and explosives, combat and noncombat vehicles, et cetera, be relocated, are you aware of that, that that actually did happen, this relocation of units from Croatia on the 10th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that did go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During that period of time, did you have any knowledge of or receive information about from the superior command the opening of artillery fire at the -- mortar fire at the units of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, frequent information of that kind would come in. So once again, I can't be specific in giving you a date when it actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the date; I'm just asking but the contents. Did you receive information of this kind generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If you look at page 2, paragraph 2 from the top, we see mention here of the Old Town, Stari Grad. Now, did information reach you about that, about what it says here in paragraph 2 related to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, information of this kind did reach us. However, I personally did not see them to be able to say specifically. But from the general information and in talking to my colleagues, that kind of thing, that's how I learned about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, the end of the document, it says that during this period of time, that was to say November, another truce was signed, one in a line of truce agreements.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to tender this document and I'd like to have a number assigned to it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is D88.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djurasic, did you hear or know or come to learn about in any way the fact that the units of the JNA during December carried out any kind of attack near Dubrovnik? Did you hear anything like that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard many times that there was some kind of fighting going on. However, I was on a different assignment in a different location, so it was very difficult for me to be able to follow and monitor the situation and know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, where were you yourself on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command post in Mokosica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And do you happen to remember when you left the command post at Mokosica to take up your new duties?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took up my new duties at the end of December. That's when I left. I don't know exactly what date it was. But I handed over my duties and went off to take up my new duties. Actually, I returned to my original duty of commander.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat, commander of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did Admiral Jokic call you over the phone on the 6th of December, and did he order you to go to Zarkovica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, there's two questions. First is, did he call? And then he's -- and then he's offering a leading question as to what certain -- what the content of the call is. Let him answer first whether or not he contacted him by telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Both propositions are valid, Mr. Rodic. But more to the point on an area so critical, you know better than to be leading. Thank you. So if you would put your first question, and then change the second after the first is asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djurasic, did you on the 6th of December contact -- did you have any contacts with Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything more about that, what those contacts were, how they came about, in what way, and the contents of your conversation?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic called me up on the phone, the official army telephone, the one we mentioned yesterday. And judging by the tone of his voice, I could tell that he was angry. I can't quite his exact words here and now. I can paraphrase them, give you the gist of it. But mostly he said, Djurasic, what's going on over there? Who is shelling Dubrovnik or opening fire and targeting Dubrovnik when I'm here talking and discussing and negotiating a truce or cease-fire? I don't know which of the two it was, what word he used. But I could tell that he was angry and excited and I said I didn't know. So that was the first intimation I had that anything was actually going on. But I said I didn't know what was going on, which I didn't. And that's where we ended our conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Before that telephone conversation with Admiral Jokic, did you have any knowledge whatsoever about the goings-on as far as combat was concerned on that particular day, or possibly about any shelling or fighting between the Croatian forces and the JNA forces?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't remember having any knowledge of that, any awareness. And that was the first time I heard about it, that something like that was going on when I spoke to the admiral.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you during that conversation with Admiral Jokic receive any orders from him?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unless you mean when he said, "What's going on?" Otherwise, any direct orders pertaining to my conduct or action on my part, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you yourself perhaps on that particular day phone Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think I did, at least I don't remember. But I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you on that day report anything to Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If we become more specific and put it this way and say, about the combat going on between the JNA units and Croatian units, did you report back to him about anything of that kind, any matters along those lines?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you on the 6th of December before that conversation with Admiral Jokic or after the conversation with Admiral Jokic go to Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't go to Zarkovica either then or -- well, I don't remember going to Zarkovica at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December, did you see Vladimir Kovacevic at all, Vladimir Kovacevic nicknamed Rambo?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd heard of him, but I never met him, nor was I ever at his positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on that 6th of December, my previous question referred to Zarkovica. I'm now asking you the same thing for Brgat and Bosanka. Did you ever go is there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Otherwise, I was on a completely different assignment, so I didn't tour those firing positions. I had no jurisdiction over them, and there was no need for me to go there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you have any jurisdiction or authority with respect to any combat unit in your environment? That is to say, coming under the command post of Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you on that day, once again, the 6th of December, report -- my question relates once again to the combat activities of the JNA units, so in that sense and along those lines, did you report about anything like that to the operational centre of the VPS at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a report did go off from the command post. I don't remember sending it myself. I had my deputies. I had my staff. They monitored the situation. So I really can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, regarding any JNA attacks, did you report on anything like that? For example, about Officer Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. There were various talks and conversations. I really can't say. What situation you mean? Are you just specifically referring to the 6th?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally did not, which does not mean that nobody did from the command post because I wasn't in my office all the time. There were other people there. So perhaps it is possible that some operational report might have been sent out, but I really don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did any of your deputies, for instance, receive an assignment from Admiral Jokic on that day?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And you as the commander of the command post and place of Mokosica, would you have been informed had somebody received a direct assignment from Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that completes my examination-in-chief of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Weiner will conduct the cross. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go back -- first, good morning, my name is Philip Weiner. I am a prosecutor with the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'm going to be asking you some questions. Now, you testified that you originally received an assignment from Captain Zec to come to Grude. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And after you received the assignment, you contacted Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you contacted him by telephone?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You contacted him because you knew him well?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you had served under him for approximately five years?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you called him because you trusted him to find out what the assignment was about?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted him to clarify the assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you trusted or you believed that he would clarify the assignment?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he told you what that assignment was?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you believed him? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you believed him because you knew him, and you knew he was a trustworthy person?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a matter of course to trust your commander whether you know him or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you knew Admiral Jokic to be an honourable man?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he was honest with you. He told you what that assignment was in Grude.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He clarified the assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you believed him because you knew him to be an honourable man?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he told you you were being sent to Grude to normalise -- basically to normalise the local situation there.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he told you that you were to help the local residents with their problems?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that -- and you were to supply the necessary resources for them?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were to feed the public?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then Admiral Jokic later sent you to Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And again, he sent you there to normalise the local situation.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were to help the local residents?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were to work with the local police?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were to feed the people?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you did that; you fed the people in Grude and Mokosica.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So while the people in the Old Town barely had any food to eat, you were feeding the people in Mokosica and Grude?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the situation in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you were feeding the people in Grude and Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just as Admiral Jokic had instructed you to do?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to move a little bit to another area. On December 8th, two officers came to see you before they were going to inspect the damage to the Old Town. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't come to see me. They had to go that way. They had to ask me to ensure safe passage for them to Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you did that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, you're familiar with the Old Town? You're familiar with the --

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was. I had been to the Old Town. I had lived in Herceg Novi for a long time, and I went to Dubrovnik frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you went there because it was a big tourist centre where everyone went?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it was a beautiful area?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the Old Town was one of the most popular destinations probably in all of Croatia, if not Yugoslavia, for tourism?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that it was a UNESCO-protected area, sir?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you met with these officers, and you got them to the Old Town. Were you aware at that time that the Old Town had been shelled, that it had been shelled on December 6th by the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see the smoke and the flames coming from the Old Town on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's because you were in Mokosica, which is about 10 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not so much the distance. It's the relief, the lay of the land that makes it impossible to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you weren't able to see it. Did you see it on television?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see the smoke pouring out of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that later on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could also see on television buildings burning?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that you knew many buildings had been damaged in the shelling by the JNA on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew from hearing from others, but what the damage was, whether many buildings were damaged, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, you knew that there were some very old buildings in the Old Town having been there as a tourist or stayed there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that the streets in the Old Town were covered in debris from these damaged buildings on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to tell you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever heard of the Old Town being in any such condition of smoke coming out, damaged buildings, buildings on fire prior to December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that. Didn't hear it from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So prior to the JNA bombing on December 6th, you hadn't heard of the Old Town being in flames or burning or buildings damaged prior to December 6th, in that type of condition?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no official information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, having visited the area, as you said, you knew that there were a lot of very old buildings.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There were old churches?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There were very old monasteries, centuries old?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There were old houses called palaces or referred to as palaces?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There was the oldest pharmacy in Europe?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The second-oldest synagogue in Europe?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know all these details, but I knew quite a lot, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that the Old Town is in a very small, congested area? All these houses are congested together?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And other than the wide Stradun, it's all of these little narrow streets that are all closely knit together?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's that kind of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, that if you shell such a place for five to ten hours, you'd have serious consequences to these old buildings?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assume the effect. If it's true that it had been shelled for such a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the effect that you can assume, it would be -- there would be serious consequences to these old or very old buildings because everything is so congested together if you shell for five to ten hours? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, you also knew that the Old Town was not a museum, but it was a living city; people were living there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that there were a number of local people who were still staying there, not everyone had left. There were a large number of local people who were staying there, who had long lived there?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that there were refugees, people who had left other areas such as Mokosica and Grude were staying with relatives and friends in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where they were exactly, in Old Town or in Dubrovnik generally. I just knew they were in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you knew a large number of people were in that area, refugees?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And once again, you know what the houses are like. They are all connected houses along these very narrow streets. It's a congested area in the Old Town. I didn't hear your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And all these palaces are tied together on these narrow, congested streets?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if you shell an area like the Old Town, which is congested with residents, for five to ten hours, that would be a dangerous situation for the local residents. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you mentioned the villages of Mokosica and Grude.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said that -- well, at the time you were placed in command of those villages, you had been an officer or a member of the JNA for about 20 years.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you a major at that time or a lieutenant colonel?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant colonel. That's when I got the rank of lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And while there, you worked with local residents starting off with Grude? You worked with the local residents.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you worked also with the local leaders who formed the crisis staff, local residents who were like the leaders of the community?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, in Mokosica; not in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you worked with the crisis staff, which was comprised of the basic -- the local leaders from the area?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the job of the crisis staff was to help the public with their day-to-day activities of life?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you discussed matters with them, you negotiated with them?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we organised life in such a way that every day in a certain period we would gather, review day-to-day problems, be it street sweeping, electricity, supply of food and necessities, and we assigned various tasks to people for the following day to make it work. But the biggest part was played by the local people who lived there because they knew the situation best. In Mokosica, for instance, it was cold. There was no firewood, no heating. And through the government of Montenegro, I managed to get two truckfuls of gas bottles. Water tanks came regularly. We managed to use power generators for a while until we got electricity restored. That was the result, the success of our efforts. And then later, life returned to normal as the service line from Mokosica to Dubrovnik started working again. And every day we would ship people there and back. That is what we did, and I hope this answer is satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what's what the local crisis staff was involved in, the day-to-day problems, food, power, wood for heating? Those are the types of matters the crisis staff is involved with, people-type issues. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I led that crisis staff, and that was our business, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you led it because Admiral Jokic had told you to do this and had told you to help these people, and you, in fact, did so?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In addition to dealing with the local residents, you had to oversee or monitor your own soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You had to make sure that the soldiers in your command were following orders, that they did what they were told to do?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's part of military discipline?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the JNA, like any other army, functions on discipline?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because if there's no discipline, then problems can arise?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if you maintain no discipline -- problems would have arisen in Mokosica and Grude if there was no military discipline.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in those areas, you were aware that there was also a military police unit?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And although it wasn't assigned to you, it was assigned to the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if a crime was committed, you would have to act. You would report the crime, notify someone up the line, but you would have to take some sort of action if a crime is committed by one of your soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that had happened, that is the most likely way in which I would have reacted. However, I had no occasion to do any such thing because the soldiers under my command had not committed a crime or done any such thing. And I had no opportunity to react to any crimes committed by a soldier or anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's because you maintained discipline?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you have to admit, if a serious crime was committed by a soldier, you would have to act?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if a soldier in your command in Grude or Mokosica raped, robbed, beat, murdered a civilian, you would have to take action?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that had happened, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you do that because if you don't take action, others might follow suit and do the same?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then if you didn't take action, the crimes would continue?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if you have a looting-type situation, if you don't take any action, other soldiers will go out and loot thinking they can get away with it, too?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And had you ever dealt with any looting-type situations in Mokosica or Grude?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, after command posts were set up and control was taken of the territory, we worked in cooperation with the police at checkpoints, and there were very, very few such incidents, although in theory it could have happened because it was a large territory with a large number of military personnel circulating. It could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, basically you took action to prevent these crimes from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. occurring?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because you know if the crimes are occurring, not only would it have negative effects on your army, lack of discipline, more people committing crimes, but it would also have a negative effect on the morale of the local population?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the locals, especially those on the crisis staff who were the local leaders, they would be complaining to you?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know there are various types of crimes, all sorts of crimes. You have looting maybe in the middle, disorderly and drunkenness on the bottom, murder and rape on the top? There are some more serious and less serious crimes than looting.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that disobeying a commander's order is a serious matter?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if someone disobeys a commander's order, it has to be dealt with or it will continue to happen?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And disobeying a commander's order to stop shelling is a serious matter, too?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if no action is taken to the disobeying of a commander's order to stop shelling, it's going to continue?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So that's why you have to use discipline and take action, as you did in Mokosica and Grude?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Targeting civilians is a serious matter?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Disobeying a commander's order and continuing to target civilians is a serious matter?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you don't take action, it will continue?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So action must be taken?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Otherwise other people, other officers will think that they can do it, too?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And targeting civilian objects is also a crime?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if that happens, someone is targeting civilian objects in violation of orders, action must be taken?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if you don't take action, it will continue?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The answer was yes? Okay. And if you don't take action, others, other officers may believe that they can do it, too?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated or you testified that you knew who Captain Kovacevic, known as Rambo, was? You know who that was? You know who he was? Not that you knew him personally --

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, I heard about him. But I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you become aware that it was Captain Kovacevic who led the attack on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How had you heard about Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from other people who talked. I heard from a report that he was a commander of a unit outside of Dubrovnik, but I didn't go to his fire position, and I didn't meet him officially as a commander. I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, did you hear that it was Captain Kovacevic's unit that shelled the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the shelling came from those positions, but all that is gossip, hearsay. I don't have any official information, and I didn't have it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, you heard that the Old Town had been shelled on December 6th. You knew of that? You learned of that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that the Old Town had been shelled for a period of five to ten hours? Shelled over that period of five to ten hours?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that shelling continued even after the command of the 19th -- 9th VPS ordered it stopped?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't know that. I didn't know when the order came, when the shelling started or when it stopped. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you know the Old Town was damaged on that date?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that people on both sides were injured on that date?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know people on both sides were killed on that date?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware a few weeks after this incident where people were hurt and killed and the Old Town was damaged and Captain Kovacevic had refused to stop shelling, after orders, that Captain Kovacevic was promoted? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever visit the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade was also involved in the shelling on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I heard some stories going round, but I really can't say. I don't know the details at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that Colonel Jovanovic was the battalion commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that because Colonel Jovanovic disobeyed orders and continued to shell, Admiral Jokic had him removed, unlike Captain Kovacevic who was promoted?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, about the personnel changes. I wasn't in the narrow staff of the command of the 9th VPS, so I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were shown Exhibit D88.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That was the letter you were shown this morning, sir. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that letter was written by Mihajlo Zarkovic who was the assistant commander for moral guidance and political propaganda. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What does the assistant commander for moral guidance and political propaganda do? What's the person's function?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. There's an error in the translation into English because the abbreviation "PP" means legal affairs, pravni poslovi, and in the B/C/S version, it is the assistant commander for MV and PP. And the translation of the PP, moral guidance and legal matters. Pravni proslovi. So the political propaganda is an error in the translation. The Defence apologies, but we would like to draw your attention to that. My learned friend interpreted it correctly as it was written, but he can check it out with the witness. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The translation that I have which I received from the Defence this morning at approximately 8.45, it says assistant commander for MV, and it says "moral guidance and PP, political propaganda."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We all have that. Mr. Rodic says that is an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, what -- the translation didn't pick up what you said. Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What position --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said pravni poslovi, legal matters or affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In this document -- actually, first, did you draft this document?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the drafting of this document?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In the letter, this assistant commander is complaining about propaganda being used by one side which he refers to as the Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is Ustasha? Isn't that a negative, slang, insulting word referring to Croatians?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood it from the text to mean, when it says Ustasha, that the forces that had the insignia of the Ustashas. And this doesn't mean to imply that all Croats are Ustashas, but certain people bearing weapons with insignia of that kind, of the -- the insignia of the Ustasha units who were referred to and called Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, or would you agree, sir, that this letter is propaganda? Propaganda is used in this letter. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the heading and title of this letter is "information," and the superior command is informing its -- these subordinate units about the situation. The situation can have a bearing on morale or moral guidance through this letter. But otherwise, it is not a letter of propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But portions of the letter contain propaganda. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, very well. You could put it that way, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Such as on the second page in the English, the sentence "this pattern of rumour spreading, misinformation, and special psychological warfare has enjoyed the active backing of certain parties and party-controlled media using their like-minded allies to openly side with the fascist forces." That's propaganda, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this as an observation most probably, with justified reasons which are not set out here. I cannot enter into the mind of the person who wrote this because it is an official document and it should be believed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it should be -- and who were the fascist forces? Would that be the Croatians?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The forces. The Croatian forces, the forces of the Croatian Army or the political forces which had that kind of fascist propaganda. One of the parties, not everybody perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said being an official document, it should be believed. That's what you just stated to a moment ago. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, on the second page, it further states: "They are setting light to car tyres around the Old Town ramparts in order to lead the press to believe that the Old Town is being shelled." Isn't that propaganda, sir?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I knew that that was true, then certainly it would be propaganda. However, I am not in a position to deny it now and say, no, tyres were not burnt, or, yes, tyres were burnt. I don't have any personal knowledge about that. But if tyres weren't burnt and this was written in such a way, then it is propaganda. Whereas if the tyres were indeed set fire to and lit, then it is a statement of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that the period just after this letter was written, and it was written on November 15th, that the Old Town had been shell for two or more days in November? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if the -- I'm sorry. There's a transcript mistake. Maybe I said it wrong. The question should have been that the Old Town had been shelled prior to this letter being written, just a few days prior to this letter being written. Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Old Town and the Old Town's harbour and its boats were shelled on November 11th and November 12th, 1991?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm the date, but I did hear about it. I heard some things along those lines. Now, whether it was on the 11th or 12th and what the intensity of it all was, it's very difficult for me to say because as I've already told you, I was occupied with other duties and information reached me on matters I did not take part in. So it was -- it's very difficult for me to say. And it would be irrelevant if I said yes or no given the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I show the witness about 45 seconds of a video of the Old Town being shelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If the witness could -- go to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, that was a video taken by war correspondent Paul Davies. You were able to see the missiles flying into the Old Town walls and into those boats, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Those weren't flying in automobile tyres that were flying in causing those boats to explode. Correct? I can't hear you, sir. Can you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see the boats burning after being struck with missiles?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any burning tyres, did you?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: For the record, that was P19, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you aware that no one was disciplined or punished after the shelling of the Old Town of Dubrovnik in November?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of anyone being punished or disciplined after the shelling of the Old Town in November?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Old Town of Dubrovnik was also shelled in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you can't recall if the JNA did, in fact, shell the Old Town in October of 1991. Had you ever hear of anyone being punished as a result of the shelling of the Old Town in October of 1991? Punished or disciplined?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it means anything to you, I didn't hear about that, but I wasn't in a position to know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, had you ever heard of anyone being punished or disciplined after the shelling in December of 1991 other than the Colonel Jovanovic, who I mentioned, who Admiral Jokic had disciplined?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't heard about Jovanovic either, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified about speaking with Admiral Jokic. Was that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the morning of December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, that was some time before noon, at about 10.00 or 11.00. I can't be more precise than that. As far as I remember, it was before noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was that the only time during the day that you can recall that you spoke with Admiral Jokic on that date?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, yes, the only time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what about on October -- I'm sorry, December 7th or 8th? Did you speak with Admiral Jokic on those dates?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when I asked you about your recollection of the time, you said "I can't be more precise than that. As far as I remember, it was before noon." That's what you said. Do you have any log concerning that telephone call? Any log or written notes in relation to that telephone call?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember just now, but the more important conversations were recorded in a diary or log of the command post. And so that archive and those documents are stored somewhere, but I don't know about that because I left, I left my duties, and I was replaced by someone else, and then again another person took his place. So I left to take up other duties, so I really can't say now. It was recorded in such and such a logbook, I really don't remember. It is more probable that it was not recorded rather than it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you since we're talking about a telephone conversation and the day's activities of twelve-and-a-half years ago, long time ago. And did you yourself --

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you yourself keep any diary or any personal records of that call or your activities on that date?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I left on my first assignment, I used the official logbook for the most part which all officers are supposed to have. And in it, the main events and assignments and decisions are noted there, and that remains as documentation and should not be taken away. So I did all that. I complied with that. When I left my duties, I left behind that official notebook or log or whatever you like. And what my replacement did, I really don't know. But I myself have no written document along those lines that I took with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you're basing your memory -- you're basing your testimony strictly on your memory today?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you recall when you spoke with Admiral Jokic that morning, he seemed upset or angry?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That there was shelling going on?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably because of that. Because that was the basic topic of our conversation, and that's why he phoned me up in the first place, probably to see whether I knew what was going on, whether I had any information as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he was trying to find out at that point what was going on, what the facts were, what was happening?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be that precise when it comes to every word he uttered. But the sense and gist of the conversation was, as I remember it, that he asked me "what's going on over there?" While I'm conducting negotiations for a truce or cease-fire, all this is going on over there. And I said I didn't know what it was all about. I heard various firing, but we were in a depression, so it was very difficult -- in a hole, so it was very difficult to say where the shooting was coming from. So that's what I remember because it was a very characteristic conversation which stuck in my mind. Now, you're asking me whether it was on the 6th or 7th or 8th, whether I had conversations or whatever, as far as I remember to the best of my recollections I did not, or perhaps it was something that I didn't consider to be essential and didn't remember. But Admiral Jokic, as I said, would come to Mokosica fairly frequently to my command post, and I would report to him about the matters that I was in charge of and would receive permission from him to go ahead with my duties, like the time when he gave me permission to take the yachts, 70 or 80 foreign yachts out of the port of Dubrovnik. We gave them permission to leave the harbour. And then with respect to the national museum, Grude, to have the artifacts returned, things like that. So we communicated more when he came to see me at my command post. I didn't go to the forward command post and report to him in the classical sense as reporting to a superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see Admiral Jokic after December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly did see him, but I can't tell you exactly when. I didn't see him that day. And most probably I didn't see him the following day either. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you do recall that he seemed tense and upset on that morning of December 6th?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way. Perhaps this is a little vulgar when I say it, but he began the conversation by swearing. He said a swear word, so I knew he was angry about what was going on because it wasn't really usual to begin our conversation in that way. So that's why it stayed in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he was trying to find -- and he was trying to obtain information from you at that time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's saying "what's going on over there?" And I said "I don't know." Perhaps he thought that I had some information about it. I really can't know what he thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you re-examine, Mr. Rodic? We could break now, but it's a question of how long you think you'll need.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, perhaps it would be better if we took a break. But of course, I won't take too long in my re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're thinking of five minutes, ten minutes, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we might finish the witness, then. He can be free. So if you'd like to press on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djurasic, linked to Document D88 that we discussed and the document you were asked about by my learned colleague, the document is entitled "information," and you said that it was the usual way, the customary way of informing subordinate units of the 9th Military Naval Sector, the 9th VPS. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The signatory is the assistant commander for moral guidance and legal affairs, Frigate Captain Mihajlo Zarkovic. That's who signed that document entitled "information."

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But he is from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Who is testifying here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's an extremely long question, Mr. Rodic, and contains a lot of facts. Perhaps you could get back to asking a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did my best to get through this quickly in view of the time. I was just reading what it says on the document. So the assistant commander recorded -- that is recorded. The document is entitled "information." So I wanted to speed matters up that way, so as to speed up the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you might get to your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Djurasic, where does all the information flow into, all the information collected about the enemy side?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object, Your Honour. That's outside the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I find it difficult, Mr. Rodic, to see that that is something that does arise from the questions that were put by Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Weiner examined the witness in detail on this document and the nature of the contents of this document. And this document contains different types of information, different areas. I asked about information about enemy forces and so on, and the document on page 1, for example, in paragraph 3 from the top contains that type of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you directed to particular and different types of information in the document asking the witness to identify what they were, you might be able to make your point, if that's -- although I don't know that you need to cross-examine to make it. The document is pretty obviously drawing on many different sources of information and dealing with very many topics. Even the Judges of the Trial Chamber can see that just looking at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Then I will move on to other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djurasic, in response to a question from my learned friend to the effect that on the 8th of December, two officers on their way to Dubrovnik were passing by, by your command post in Mokosica on their way to do some filming. You said it's true.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what exactly did they say about their mission?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radojkovic, Bosko, Lieutenant Colonel, was in the same class with me, and there was another officer with him, told me that they were going to film the damage incurred to Dubrovnik during the shelling. They had a videocamera. The Croatian side allowed it, and they went off.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you who sent them on that mission?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it was the command of the 9th naval sector. It was just my supposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how they were dressed on the 8th of December?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On their way back to Dubrovnik, did they go the same way? Did they pass by you again?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They waited for transportation and left back for the command post. We had a short conversation. I remember asking Boskovic, "what's the situation?" He said "there is damage, but it's not that bad." That's what he said. And I didn't go any further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was your impression when he told you about the damage that he had seen there? Did he speak about or describe the damage?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly now. I know that it didn't sound dramatic the way he said it because otherwise I would have remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, while you were at the Mokosica command post, you referred at one point to the crisis staff when you were responding to my learned friend. Tell me, what was the crisis staff in Mokosica all about? Who was in it? What were its tasks? Who organised it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already in existence when I arrived in Mokosica. We didn't want to change the name, but we adjusted its operation to what I believed to be the priorities. And the people who were there, with a few exceptions, such as Mr. Bonic, Mr. Zdravko Bosnan, and some others whose names I don't recall now held a meeting together with me, and at that first meeting we determined -- we identified our priorities, what had to be done first.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said with a few exceptions, did anyone from the previous crisis staff leave when the army arrived?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe I gathered from their conversation that some people had left. And I let it go because I didn't want to have too many people on the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, did anyone on the crisis staff in Mokosica with whom you cooperated and where you worked wear the uniform of the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did that crisis staff in Mokosica had any units of the Croatian forces understood its control or command or did it cooperate with any?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Djurasic. Your Honours, I have finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Rodic. Colonel, may we thank you for your presence here and the evidence you've given. You'll be pleased to know that you may now go and go back to your home and continue with your life. So thank you, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have a break now to enable -- because of the unusual hours we're sitting today, we will resume at 1.15 to give people a chance to have a quick bite to eat. And could I indicate that we expect to finish, depending just where the evidence of a particular witness is, we would expect to finish at about 4.00 this afternoon. So we'll resume at 1.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we start, if I can just assist the Chamber on P19 this morning, to give you the times that were involved, it might be helpful to direct you. It was 6.10 -- between 6.10 and 7.24 on that piece of video. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It will now be on the record. The next witness, Mr. Rodic or Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence calls Tomislav Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jovanovic. Would you take the card --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and make the affirmation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I should like you to tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tomislav Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, Mr. Jovanovic, what you are by profession at present.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At present, I'm a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was your profession previously?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Previously, I was an officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what rank did you hold when you retired?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, something about your education. What education have you had? What schools have you graduated from?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from primary and elementary school, and a school for NCOs, and then the academy for the ground forces, land forces, and finally the command staff academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the military schools you graduated from.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the school for subofficers or noncommissioned officers, and then I went to the military academy of the land forces and the command staff academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, briefly, where you served during your military career.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: During my military career, I served in practically all the republics of the former Yugoslavia with the exception of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, did you serve in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And that was during the latter period prior to my retirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, where did you serve in Montenegro and since when?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I served in Montenegro from 1983 working at the command of the 9th Naval Sector until 1996 when I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From 1983 to 1996, what duties did you discharge in the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was chief of engineering.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what engineering units were in existence within the framework of the 9th Naval Sector? Let us limit ourselves to years 1990 and 1991.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the 9th Naval Sector, there was one engineering unit, and it was the engineering battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That engineering battalion, did it have a special emblem or a number?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the 130th Engineering Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown D46.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, please look at the ELMO. This is a diagram of the 9th Naval Sector. And please tell us if you see your unit in this diagram.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please show it on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please look at the other units enumerated under the 9th Naval Sector. Can you confirm that they were also part of this sector in autumn 1991? Do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was your role as chief of engineers of the 9th Naval Sector in the period when you occupied this post?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Within the framework of the 9th Naval Sector, my duties included making proposals for the use of the engineers' unit to my commander, taking care of its training, of the personnel and officers in the unit. Because I was the direct link between the commander and the unit, and the unit was subordinated to the sector commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did you perform these duties in October, November, December 1991 as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I discharged these duties in the said months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what is the composition of an engineers battalion, that particular, 130th?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The battalion consisted of the command, the first pioneer, the second pioneer companies, the engineers company, a scouting platoon, communications section, and logistical platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, how is an engineers battalion used, on whose orders?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The use of an engineers battalion is made upon the orders of the commander, in this specific case, the commander of the 9th Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, can the battalion commander use the units of this engineers battalion in circumvention of the orders of the commander of the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. He could through me, but I would have to inform the commander in advance and make my proposal on how to use the battalion professionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could a chief of staff instead of the commander issue an order to use the battalion?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In autumn 1991, who was the commander of the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander was Admiral Miodrag Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the same period, who was chief of staff of the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of staff of the 9th Naval Sector was Milan Zec, captain of warship.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
