utterances.text: As part of the regular activities of the command of the 9th Naval Sector, are reporting sessions organised?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, usually at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who attends these sessions, these briefings?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Unit commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You say unit commanders. Which units?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Those subordinated to the 9th Naval Sector, and representing the command, there would be the commander or chief of staff and operative officers and chiefs of arms and services.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What did these briefings look like in the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the largest unit would begin. Briefings would be made verbally, followed by written reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: After the reports made by commanders of subordinated units, what would happen at the briefing?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: After reports were received from subordinated units, the decision and orders would be issued for the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: By the commander of the 9th Naval Sector or by the chief of staff or the most senior officer present at the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the 9th Naval Sector sent any reports to anyone else, regular, daily reports, combat reports or operative reports? For instance, in the period we are discussing, to whom would such reports be sent?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The command of the 9th Naval Sector would draw up an operative report and send it to its superior command. In this instance, it would be the 2nd Operations Group, the General Staff, and their naval district.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who chaired these briefings at the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Usually the commander of the sector, the chief of staff, or, if they were absent, somebody from the operations section.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the 2nd Operational Group is?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That is a temporary category envisioned to encompass the units in the territory where we were located. It commanded through the 9th Naval Sector and all the other units subordinated to that command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Another matter, if you know: How was this unit mobilised, the 130th Engineers Battalion?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was formed through the organs of command of the 9th Naval Sector following mobilisation and through the battalion command which actually carried out the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that at one point in the course of the autumn 1991, some combat operations began, carried out by the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that in autumn 1991, the 9th Naval Sector carried out certain combat operations?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It did. After the mobilisation was completed, when the units were mobilised, an incident occurred involving the Croatian Army or provoked by the Croatian Army followed by an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In October, November, December, where was the command of the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the combat operations, the command of the 9th Naval Sector was in Grude for a short time. And after that, it was located in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In that same period, October, November, December, where was the command of the 130th Engineers Battalion?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was behind the first defence lines quartered in Mlini, Astarea Hotel, Astarea Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In Mlini, at the place where the battalion command was, was the supply of equipment and materiel also organised?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Everything we needed to conduct these combat operations that we didn't have on the spot was supplied from warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that there was a field warehouse of materiel and equipment organised at that very location?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a storage place was organised for mines and explosives, and it was secured. Ignition devices, according to regulation, were placed on one side, and mines and explosives on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In October, November, December 1991, what were the most frequent tasks assigned to your unit, the 130th Engineers Battalion?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The tasks of the engineers units are to build and maintain and repair roads, to build obstacles, for instance, lay mines, and to build fortifications. Those are the three main tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me something about road repairs that you mentioned. Do you know of a place where the road was damaged in this period?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do. First of all, at the beginning of our combat operations, the road was damaged close to the hydropower stations -- station called Plat in the area of Kupari. Our battalion followed the troops that went through this area in the course of combat operations. Infantry units could circumvent this section of the road, but other units that had vehicles could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At one point, did you receive orders to repair the road in that stretch?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we received orders to repair the road as soon as possible so that units on the front line could be supplied with food, ammunition, and all the other necessities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, who issued orders for the road to be repaired?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The sector commander did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether there was any firing?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when the engineers unit came to repair that section of the road, it was targeted from the area of Kupari. And at the beginning, the shells fell along the coastal belt, and the people doing the work thought that there wasn't -- they didn't have the weapons to jeopardise the lives of the people engaged in the repair work. However, when the shells flew over the heads of the people repairing the roads, when they saw that happening, they stopped the repairs. And when it grew dark, they continued so that the road was, in fact, reconstructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told us a moment ago that the order to repair the road was issued by the sector commander. Who was the sector commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was Admiral Miodrag Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was the road repaired anywhere else during this period, on any other section?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As our units advanced, so the Croatian units destroyed the roads to prevent the troops from reaching them. So the roads had to be repaired in the area of Brgat, or rather towards the Dubrovacka Rijeka area, and later on around Mokosica, and later on in depth around Slano.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, in the area of Mokosica specifically, was the road repaired there?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the road was repaired there, and we had losses of technical equipment; that is to say, the loader, the mechanical device, the loader that was working there, it was known as the 160, and the man manning the machine stepped on a mine with his front and rear wheel, so he was -- it was blown up and damaged. So I want to say that in addition to the destruction done to the road, the surrounding area was mined. Anti-tank and anti-infantry mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who laid these mines?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The mines were laid by the soldiers belonging to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did your unit have any other assignments to give assistance to the civilian population on the territory they were in?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since the engineers battalion was situated in a place called Mlini, not far from Kupari, in the Astarea Hotel, elderly people remained there, elderly men and women were still there, and so were some children. So in the place we took our meals, and we had to supply our own meals for the battalion, and we did the cooking within the battalion and didn't have to rely on any logistics for the unit's food, so we fed the people who found themselves there. They had no other means of livelihood or way of coming by food.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, during this period of time when we're talking about October, November, and December of 1991, in your particular unit, what was the situation like as far as discipline was concerned?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The engineers unit is a highly disciplined unit, especially since it works with explosive devices and construction machinery, engineering machinery. So they are very well used to a high level of discipline, and there were no transgressions that would have had an adverse effect on the population, anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might the witness be shown Document D61 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, would you take a look at the document, and point 2 in particular, and the first line of that paragraph, read it out.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, is this a document dated the 5th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This refers to repairs done in the Slano area, the Slano Road, and the section of the road at Sitnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this in fact a report of the command of the 9th VPS dated the 5th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this a command report? Is this a report by the command of the 9th VPS dated the 5th of December 1991? Take a look at it, please. Take a look at the entire document before you, first, please. Is it a regular combat report?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it says 1700 hours on the 5th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, now, please, the work going on mentioned as being performed by the engineers unit, does it correspond to your recollections of what the unit was engaged in during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does correspond to that, especially construction of the Sitnica section of the road on the territory of Montenegro. A road was being built to establish better connection between -- because there was no view from Leotar, so a relay station was positioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The members of your unit, or rather, the 130th engineers battalion, those men, at the beginning of December, that means, the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th of December, were they working on any engineering work, construction work, in the vicinity of the town of Dubrovnik itself?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not in the immediate vicinity of Dubrovnik, no. We weren't working there. The construction work was being done mostly at the request of the subordinate units. I cannot remember all the details involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At around the 6th of December, perhaps the 5th or 7th of December, round about that time, was the engineers battalion engaged in any work at Brgat or Bosanka or Mokosica or some other area like that as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the region of Brgat and Bosanka, no, it was not. I don't think it was. Whereas we had completed our work in the Mokosica area when our vehicle was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us where on the 6th of December most of the members of your 130th Engineers Battalion were.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the men in the 130th Engineers Battalion were located in the region around the place called Mlini.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you yourself, Mr. Jovanovic, where were you, if you remember, on that 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, the 6th of December 1991, I was at the forward command post in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the course of that day, did you receive any orders?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of that day, I did receive an order from the duty officer up at the forward command post, and an order coming from the chief of staff to prepare a certain quantity of explosives and to bring them to the Zarkovica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you said that an order had come in from the chief of staff. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was Warship Captain Milan Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, specifically what Captain Milan Zec ordered you to do. What was the order he gave you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I received the order from the duty officer, and he told me that I was to prepare explosives, explosive devices, half a kilogram -- packaged in half-kilogram lots, a slow-burning fuse, and to give it to a unit to bring into Zarkovica. So that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What did you do once you had received that order? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When I received the order, I went to the battalion command where the battalion was deployed, and I conveyed the order to the battalion commander. I told him what we were supposed to do. And then we started preparing the devices that had been requested by the chief of staff. So that once we had got all these items together, we loaded them up into a vehicle --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we'll come to that. Thank you. Tell me, please, what did you use these explosive devices for, the ones you were ordered to prepare?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assumed that that materiel would be used to destroy some firepower positions targeting our own forces at Zarkovica from the Srdj area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So with these packages of plastic explosives that you had, what type of target would be best destroyed using that type of explosive?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't plastic explosives. They were ordinary explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Ordinary explosives.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably they were supposed to destroy the firepower positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, his previous answer is "I assume that the materiel would be used." He says that on line 22, page 51. And again, "probably they were used." He's just making assumptions or speculating. If he doesn't know, he shouldn't be allowed to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, if you want to press the matter, you'd better see if there is actual knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Once you received the order to prepare this materiel, did you know what the materiel would be used for, what purpose?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know what it was going to be used for. I could only assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what did you assume?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may we hear what the witness assumed? I don't see any objection there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the relevance of what this witness assumed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance, Your Honour, is that he is a professional in the field of explosive devices, so he could know, he is well-placed to know what such packages of explosives could be used for. That's what we're dealing with, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you want to get from him what were the possible uses of such packaged explosives, go ahead. But not to assume what the use actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was never my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, your question would have guided him in the wrong direction then, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, so what would packaged explosives of this kind be used for?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we had packaged explosives like that, we could use them to destroy bunkers, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take you to prepare all this materiel, all these explosive devices, to get them together?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we needed about one to two hours to get the explosive devices together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, once you'd completed your preparations, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When we completed our preparations, we placed the explosive devices in the vehicle. The vehicle was a Pinzgauer, and the men along with it, and we started out towards Srdj. And we reached Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what happened when you reached Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When we reached Zarkovica, we were stopped by two soldiers, and they said to us -- they asked us where we were going, in fact. We said we were on our way, that we had received orders from the chief of staff to take the explosives -- to bring in the explosive devices. And the two soldiers said that those explosives, the ones we had with us, were no longer needed. And that we could take them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I listened to what the soldiers told us, and we returned those explosives. So the explosives that we got together were never used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what time of day, or rather I withdraw that question. Tell me, first, how far you'd gone, what point had you reached? Had you actually reached Zarkovica on that day at all?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We reached -- we almost reached Zarkovica, not quite. We were a little in front of Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what time of day it was, if you happen to recall? What time was it? I mean, when you approached Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon, sometime between 1400 hours and 1500 hours, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that it was in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Because during that period of time, it began to grow dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point on the 6th of December 1991 go to the observation post on Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December 1991, were you at any time in Brgat or Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, apart from the time when I went there with explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December 1991, did you at any point talk to Admiral Miodrag Jokic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December 1991, did you receive any orders from Admiral Miodrag Jokic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: After the 6th of December, did Admiral Miodrag Jokic interrogate you on the events of the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, three questions in a row leading in relation to Admiral Jokic. There is no testimony that Admiral Jokic contacted him on those dates, spoke to him on those dates, and there's no testimony that Admiral Jokic interrogated him on that date. This evidence is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't see it on that basis that I can take a view, that the Chamber can take a view that it is not relevant to the Defence. It may not be relevant to the Prosecution case. But the question can be asked, and we will learn the relevance perhaps in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, after the 6th of December, did Admiral Jokic ever interrogate you on the events on Srdj of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic and I never discussed it, and he never asked me anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever give a written statement to Admiral Jokic concerning the events of the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any relations with Captain Vladimir Kovacevic? Did you have any connection with the events on Srdj of the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I had no contact at all, unless you mean the previous days when I went to inspect the unit and see how well it was fortified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Colonel, you were contacted on December 6th by the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he told you that Captain Zec had told him to contact you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did he -- and did they say at that time that Captain Zec was on Zarkovica at the observation post, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they say if Captain Kovacevic was there at the time, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose he was at his command post, but I don't know where he was in relation to his subordinated unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they say that Colonel Kovacevic was there at the time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you weren't up there, so you really can't tell who was up there at the time? You just received a phone call. You can't say for sure who was up there.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you told to come to Zarkovica with the materiel?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The order was that the engineers unit should come with the explosives that we had prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you actually went there with those explosives later in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went there personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were supposed to be there except for being stopped in transit?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then you testified you never got to Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I got to Zarkovica, but the explosives and the rest that I was carrying was never used. We returned it back to the unit, to the field storage where we had taken it from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You just stated that you got to Zarkovica. Did you actually go on to the mountain? Did you walk into the command post?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you weren't present -- since you weren't on Zarkovica, you weren't present for any of the telephone calls or radio communications that were being made from Zarkovica during that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you weren't present for any calls that Captain Zec made from Zarkovica that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Since you weren't on Zarkovica at the command post, you weren't present for any telephone calls that Captain Zec made from that location?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I certainly wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you don't know what, if anything, Captain Zec or the other officers said to Admiral Jokic during that afternoon from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You don't know if Admiral Jokic was told that you were on the way to Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You don't know that Admiral Jokic was told that you'd be on Zarkovica very shortly?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You don't know who else on that command post was told that you were on the way?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you don't know who those people, who were told that you were on the way, spoke to?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So several people might have believed that you were on Zarkovica or on the way to Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They could have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you weren't the only Colonel Jovanovic within the 2nd Operational Group. There were others.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, was there a Colonel Miodrag Jovanovic? Miroslav Jovanovic? Are you familiar with him?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not a colonel. He was a major.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what about the Jovanovic --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And there was also a Colonel Vojislav Jovanovic. And I'm Tomislav Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The other Jovanovic, where was he located?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since there are three Jovanovics, if that is the drift of the questions, could the Prosecutor please name these three persons exactly and refer to an exact period of time for which this is relevant so as not to confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the time, Mr. Weiner, is relevant. The witness may well be able to tell us names as well as yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where was Colonel Vojislav Jovanovic on December 6th, if you know? What unit was he assigned to?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I could not tell you where he was. But I believe he had come from the Territorial Defence of Montenegro on some sort of special mission that involved certain assignments and duties, but I'm not really aware of what assignments. He was not part of the 9th Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was he the Jovanovic who used the nickname Kurd, Kurd Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you recently speak with another witness, a Slobodan Novakovic, where you two discussed this Kurd Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not discuss him. He was a simple soldier in the Territorial Defence, so we didn't discuss these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you recently stay in the same facility as Defence witness Slobodan Novakovic within the past week?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And while there, did you speak with Mr. Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you discuss this, the matters of this case or Dubrovnik with him?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did talk in general, but nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall speaking to him about this other Jovanovic, Tomislav.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am Tomislav.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The other Novakovic, Vojislav. Jovanovic, I'm sorry. The other one, Kurd Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, are you certain, sir, that you weren't on Zarkovica on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from bringing the explosives, I was not there for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're certain you weren't at the observation post on December 6th at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, Defence counsel has submitted an exhibit, D71, which indicates that at the observation post, he, which is referring to Captain Soldo, saw the commander, Vladimir Kovacevic, captain of the battleship vessel, Milan Zec, Colonel Gavrilo Kovacevic and Colonel Jovanovic? So my question to you is again: Are you sure you were not on at the observation post on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move on to a few other subjects. Maybe we'll come back to that. Now, you indicated that your unit was mainly involved in road repair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that you had to repair damaged roads because the military needed the roadways.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So road repair for your unit was a military activity.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you needed those roadways to transport food, ammunition, and supplies to the troops. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also indicated that your engineering unit was highly disciplined.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said because of that, there was no adverse effects on the local population.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You also indicated that -- or let me ask you, you know as a career soldier that discipline must be maintained in armies. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And people must follow orders; soldiers must follow the orders that they're given.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Otherwise if orders aren't being followed, you just have anarchy?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you use discipline to ensure that orders are followed.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you use discipline to ensure -- I'm sorry, your last answer didn't come through. Could you repeat that. The question was: You use discipline to ensure that orders are followed.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if orders are not followed, you have to deal with it, whether punish or take some action against a person.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Otherwise, the lack of discipline continues.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if you don't punish an act or if you don't punish a crime, it will continue.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And others will follow suit and commit the same crimes or acts seeing that no one else is being punished. You nodded your head yes. Could you --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And disobeying orders is a serious violation.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if someone is told not to shell a certain area and they do that, that's a serious violation. That's a disobeyment of orders.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if someone disobeys that type of order, you must act immediately so it doesn't happen again.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Otherwise, it will continue to happen.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Old Town was shelled in October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that it had been shelled. I didn't see it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you heard it had been shelled by the JNA in October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you hear of anyone being punished or disciplined for shelling the Old Town in October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that anybody was punished.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that the Old Town was shelled in October of -- I'm sorry, in November of 1991 by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer with any certainty. But from that area, that's also something I heard, our positions were shelled, the positions on Mount Zarkovica and the positions where Captain Kovacevic was located. Rumour had it that it was shelled from Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Once again, my question is: Did you hear that the Old Town of Dubrovnik, just the Old Town, was shelled in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that it had been shelled, but I didn't see anything, and I cannot tell you anything with great certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine. And as a result of that shelling, did you hear of anyone being punished or disciplined, any JNA officers being punished or disciplined, after that shelling in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, were you aware that the Old Town of Dubrovnik was shelled on December 6th, 1991, by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew because I learned from my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: From where you were located on the outskirts of Zarkovica, could you see the smoke and the flames coming out of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I could not see because it is much lower than the facility at Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned -- well, let me ask you one more question before we get off that. Did you hear of anyone being punished or disciplined after the December 6th shelling of the Old Town by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the unit commanded by Captain Kovacevic was the unit that shelled the Old Town on December 6th, 1991? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you also hear or did you also learn that approximately two weeks after the shelling of the Old Town on December 6th, about two weeks later, on or about December 22nd, 1991, Captain Kovacevic was promoted?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you testified today that the 9th Naval Sector sent reports up to the 2nd Operational Group. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Operational Group was Pavle Strugar, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who was his chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean at the operational group?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was General Radomir Damjanovic, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also said that the 2nd Operational Group was a temporary creation; that's what you testified to. You used the word "temporary."

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And by the word "temporary," you don't mean a number of days or a number of weeks.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, sorry. I meant the temporary personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And by "temporary," it could have been months, it could be years or a year that these people were in this operation?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it could.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because as you know, the 2nd Operational Group was in existence in October of -- let's start off, September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: October of 1991? November of 1991? December of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So we're not talking about something temporary just a few days or a few weeks?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, I'd like to show you a document, Document D47.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you look at that document, please. Sir, you've had a chance to look at the document. That document is to the command of the 9th VPS from Commander Lieutenant Colonel Pavle Strugar. And in that document, he issues a number of orders.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he issues those orders to the command of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the commander of the 9th VPS is Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So this letter involves Pavle Strugar on the 18th of November 1991 issuing orders to Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it indicates one of the orders is not to fire on the Old Town, order number 4.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That order wasn't followed in December of 1991. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that order wasn't followed in November of 1991.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Nor was that order followed in October of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Weiner. But the order is dated the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can hardly say it's not followed in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of orders in the autumn of 1991, other than this one, not to fire upon the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the order from the superior command was that the town of Dubrovnik should not be targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And those orders were not followed, as you've testified, in October and November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as you also testified, no one was punished or disciplined for those violations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said that he did not know whether anybody was punished or disciplined.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of whether anybody was disciplined or punished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine. Sorry about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as you stated, you were not aware of anyone ever being punished or disciplined for violations of those orders?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you weren't just a minor soldier; you were a unit commander. You're a colonel and the commander of the engineering unit at that time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a colonel and chief of the engineers. The commander of the engineers unit was somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were chief of the engineers. And as chief of the engineers and a colonel, you were not aware of anyone being punished for violating the order of not to bomb the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say you don't remember that, you don't recall or you don't remember anyone being punished. I want the transcript to be --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit D44, please. Your Honour, it's a long document. It's close to break time. Could the witness be allowed to read the document over the break, and we could use a quick break at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That would be a more efficient use of time. We will have the 20-minute break now --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you get a chance to look at that document?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I just want to go through it very quickly. It's a document to the General Staff of the Republic of Yugoslavia from the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, then Commander Sokic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And Commander Sokic says that he has decided upon a plan of attack?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he lists the assignments of the units that will be involved in the command of that attack which are also units of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the 9th VPS is given certain assignments and tasks as part of that attack.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because the 9th VPS was subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all. Just a couple other quick matters, and we'll be finished. Now, on December 6th when you were called for certain materiel, certain types of bombs, it took you some time to put it together. You said it took you one to two hours to put the explosives together?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you surprised by the sudden call for these explosives?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, you didn't anticipate the need for these explosives. They weren't ready and available.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They weren't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, you were surprised by the military action that was occurring on December 6th, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You weren't aware ahead of time that there would be a military occurring on December 6th? You weren't aware on the 4th or 5th of December?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, speaking of December 6th, were you ever ordered to appear before the command of the 2nd Operational Group or appear before General Strugar to be interviewed concerning the -- your activities on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the 2nd Operational Group ever question you or members of your unit about the activities of December 6th?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the 2nd Operational Group ever question you as to why you were being called to Zarkovica? Why you had been called to Zarkovica on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did anyone from the command of the 2nd Operational Group ever question you about the actions of the engineering unit on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I have one moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, during that period we have been discussing, October, November, December, did you, for instance, in December hear that Croatian forces were firing at the JNA from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the month of November, did you hear that Croatian forces were firing on the JNA from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear the same thing in October, that Croatian units were firing at the JNA from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. It's all outside the scope of cross-examination. Move to strike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, I would take the opposite view, I'm afraid, Mr. Weiner. Responsive to. Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. With the assistance of the usher -- just a second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, what exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D44. The same exhibit that the witness has just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, is that the document you've just read?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at para 1 of that document. Does it say anywhere in this directive, in that document, that the assignment of the units of the 2nd Operational Group is to capture the town of Dubrovnik? Or does it speak only of a blockade?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Blockade only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Has the order ever been given to take hold, to capture Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is anything like that stated in the document that you've already had occasion to read?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the time -- I withdraw this question. Let us go back, Mr. Jovanovic, briefly, to the 6th of December. You said that you were at the forward command post of the 9th Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you told personally by the duty officer at the command post of the 9th Naval Sector of the orders issued by the Warship Captain Zec?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did the duty officer tell you personally that the order comes from the captain of the warship, Mr. Zec?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This order from Captain Zec, did it come to the forward command post in Kupari, the forward command post of the 9th Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reason to suspect that the duty officer of the 9th Naval Sector was not conveying to you the orders of the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There was no questioning as to the validity of the orders. There was no questioning as to Kupari, as to his receipt of the orders. These are outside the scope of cross-examination again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want to take a very narrow view of the issues that you raised by your cross-examination. I'm afraid I don't agree again. Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Jovanovic, have any reason to suspect that the operative officer on duty of the 9th Naval Sector was not conveying to you the orders of the captain of the warship Zec on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I had no reason to suspect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was the situation completely normal, as usual?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That is all I have for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Djurasic, you'll be pleased -- Jovanovic, I do beg your pardon. Mr. Jovanovic, I think you'll be pleased to know that that's the end of your evidence. We would like to thank you for the assistance you've given, and you're free now to return to your home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there another witness at the moment, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately we don't have any more witnesses for today. We apologise to the Chamber and to our learned friends for not having prepared any more witnesses. But our next witness is coming tomorrow morning. I also wish to avail myself of this opportunity to inform the Chamber that in view of the speed of the examination of Defence witnesses, we are going to increase the planned number of witnesses for next week so that we ensure expedient work until the end of this month -- the month of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Don't forget that the plan is for four weeks of evidence, not to the end of July, which would be five weeks. So keep that in mind. What concerns the Chamber, of course, Mr. Petrovic, is that there are two lengthy expert witnesses who can be expected, and there's also the question of whether the accused will be giving evidence. Is there any decision about that at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the accused shall not testify in his case for reasons that are well known. The Defence is not prepared to take this chance or responsibility involved in having a man testify with the kind of psychological and other problems that our client has because that also involves significant effort in testifying, plus undergoing cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the right and entitlement of the accused, and that, of course, is respected. Its effect is to lessen the concern of the capacity to complete the list. But it still must be expected that the cross-examination of some of these witnesses will be of some length. So we will need to be conscious that we don't lose time in future weeks. This being the first week, clearly it's very difficult at the beginning to judge just how slowly or quickly the proceedings may go. So we will treat this week as a learning experience. Very well. Now, the one witness available for tomorrow, you anticipated for your examination some one and a half hours. Is that still the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I shall lead the examination-in-chief of tomorrow's witness. Our estimate was an hour and a half. However, this witness arrived in The Hague late. He did not come with that first group. And he also brought some documents that might make his examination longer in view of the scope of facts he will be speaking to so that at this point we believe we could complete the examination-in-chief sometime during the second session of tomorrow's hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have a capacity to anticipate my every thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I am flattered. Your Honour, the Defence did raise the matter of new documents that are not on the exhibit list, and I don't know that they will be sought to be exhibited. However, we have not yet received them, nor have we been given any lead information about which documents from the existing exhibit list may be sought to be introduced. So it would be helpful, I think, certainly for us to get that as soon as possible, and then obviously we will do everything we can to try to jump in quickly and have a crisp, expeditious cross. But we are very much in the dark right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The pace that you have been setting with the past few witnesses has been excellent, and we encourage it. My first concern is whether we will need the full period tomorrow, or whether it would be more practical to have a slightly late start and yet be sure of finishing the witness tomorrow. I'm at the moment not entirely clear. Mr. Rodic, it would probably help you most if we had a slightly later start. Can we be confident of finishing the witness, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, in view of the tempo of the cross-examination demonstrated by our learned friends of the Prosecution during this week, I feel confident that it would be realistic to expect that the testimony of that witness, too, would be finished during the course of the day tomorrow because we don't have a witness for Friday. This is the fifth witness planned for this first week of trial. So we thought that along with the opening statements, we would have one witness per day, so that will, in fact, be the last witness we're going to call this week. And as for the next group of witnesses, they are arriving on Saturday for the following week, and there will be more witnesses there, not to waste any of our valuable time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My immediate concern, Mr. Rodic, is whether the full day will be needed tomorrow, the full ordinary sitting day, or whether we could have a slightly later start.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know how much later. Can you give me an assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Half an hour or an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Half an hour, if we start half an hour later, then I think, yes, we'll be realistically able to get through the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will then commence at 9.30 tomorrow. You have heard, Mr. Rodic, the plea of Ms. Somers to learn about the documentary exhibits for tomorrow. You understand that that will facilitate preparation and the speed of tomorrow. Can we broaden that inquiry. The witness summaries and so on, are they to become available for the future witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for your first question with respect to documents, it is true that the Prosecution has not been supplied with the new documents that we have. They won't be tendered, all of them. And we already discussed this with the Prosecution, and we did promise that during the afternoon we would provide them with those documents to give them sufficient time to prepare for tomorrow's proceedings. As for the summaries, witness statements and summaries of those for next week, next week's group of witnesses, as I have already said, arrive on Saturday, and we'll do our best over the weekend to write up those summaries on the contents of their testimony to inform our colleagues of the Prosecution thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any other matter that either counsel needs to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do wish to inquire, if, for whatever reason, perhaps because of surprise, for example, we need to carry on for a bit on Friday, albeit not a new witness, was the Chamber anticipating simply finishing the witness direct and cross and redirect tomorrow, or is Friday still a calendared day in the event we need to have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Friday will remain a day for sitting until it's clear that we don't need it. Whatever else happens, we must finish the witness that remains that is available to ensure, then, that we can make a prompt start with the further witnesses on Monday. But the indications are we should finish the evidence of this fifth witness in the course of tomorrow, even though we start at 9.30. Very well. We will adjourn now and commence again at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of July, 2004, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.32 p.m.,
